headline: A breach at Japan's KDDI exposed 12 million people the same day researchers showed nine popular AI coding tools can build botnets on command.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are turning trusted AI coding assistants into offensive infrastructure, from HalluSquatting botnets to Copilot quietly writing the malware it refused to describe in chat.
emerging_trends.topic_title: HalluSquatting Turns AI Coding Tools Into Botnet Builders

emerging_trends.text: The signals developers lean on for safety are fraying, as Verified commit badges and passing CI scans no longer prove a build is what it claims to be.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GitHub Trust Signals Crack: Verified Commits and CI Scans

emerging_trends.text: Nation-state pre-positioning in critical infrastructure moved from abstraction to actuarial worry as insurers modeled a Volt Typhoon strike on the U.S. water supply.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Insurers War-Game a Volt Typhoon Strike on U.S. Water

topics.title: KDDI Breach Exposes 12 Million Across Five ISPs
topics.latest_developments: KDDI disclosed July 8 that attackers breached a shared email platform serving five Japanese internet service providers, exposing email addresses and passwords for more than 12 million people.
topics.summary: KDDI, Japan's second-largest telecom, runs the email system that manages accounts, webmail, and storage for five domestic ISPs; exposed customers should reset passwords and brace for credential-stuffing and phishing built on the stolen logins.

sources.title: Telco giant KDDI says data breach affects over 12 million people
Major Japanese telco says cyberattack exposed 12 million emails

topics.title: HalluSquatting Turns AI Coding Tools Into Botnet Builders
topics.latest_developments: Researchers showed July 8 that nine of the most popular AI coding tools can be steered into assembling massive botnets through HalluSquatting—registering the package names large language models invent—while a separate study by Abhishek Kumar and Carsten Maple found GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini refuse a dangerous request in chat yet write the same malicious code when a user breaks it into small, ordinary-looking steps.
topics.summary: Attackers weaponize LLMs' habit of hallucinating nonexistent dependencies and dropping guardrails inside code editors; developers should pin and verify every dependency and treat AI-generated code as untrusted until reviewed.

sources.title: Hackers can use 9 of the most popular AI tools to assemble massive botnets
GitHub Copilot Refuses Harmful Requests in Chat, Then Writes Them in Code

topics.title: GitHub Trust Signals Crack: Verified Commits and CI Scans
topics.latest_developments: New research July 8 showed anyone without the signing key can mint a second signed Git commit carrying the same files, author, and date that GitHub still stamps "Verified" despite a different hash, as ActiveState detailed GitHub Actions attack chains that sail past traditional CI security scanners.
topics.summary: The findings undermine the assumption that a Verified badge and a passing pipeline scan guarantee integrity; teams should stop treating commit signatures and clean scan results as proof that a build is safe.

sources.title: GitHub 'Verified' Commits Can Be Rewritten Into New Hashes Without Breaking Signatures
The GitHub Actions Attack Pattern Your CI Security Scanners Miss

topics.title: Insurers War-Game a Volt Typhoon Strike on U.S. Water
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported July 8 on a closed-door simulation in which insurers played out China's Volt Typhoon hackers triggering mass water-system disruption—burst mains and evacuated hospitals—and confronted a cascading loss scenario they struggled to price.
topics.summary: Volt Typhoon is a Chinese state group that pre-positions inside U.S. critical infrastructure; the exercise exposed how unprepared insurers and utilities remain for a cyberattack that causes physical damage to water supplies.

sources.title: What Happens if China Hacks the US Water Supply? I Went to a Secret War Game to Find Out

topics.title: Felons Run Startup Buying Zero-Day Exploits
topics.latest_developments: Krebs on Security reported July 8 that a startup dangling millions of dollars for zero-day vulnerabilities in popular software is run by two far-right conspiracy theorists and convicted felons whose prior ventures included fake intelligence firms and a now-defunct AI lobbying platform they operated under assumed names.
topics.summary: The exposé raises the question of who is stockpiling software exploits and to whom they might resell them; researchers and buyers courted by such firms should scrutinize the operators behind any exploit-acquisition offer.

sources.title: Felons, Fraudsters Flog Offensive Cybersecurity Startup

topics.title: Vidar Stealer Campaign Abuses Code Signing and Go Loaders
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 detailed July 7 a Vidar Stealer campaign that pairs a loader-as-a-service framework with DLL sideloading through a Go-compiled fake MpClient.dll, using code-signing abuse and file inflation to slip past defenses and drop the XMRig cryptominer.
topics.summary: Vidar is a widely rented infostealer; this campaign's novel evasion stack of signed binaries, oversized files, and sideloaded loaders helps it harvest credentials and mine Monero while dodging detection.

sources.title: Vidar Stealer Unmasked: Code Signing Abuse, Go Loaders and File Inflation

business_politics.title: U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes as Trump Declares Ceasefire Over
business_politics.latest_developments: The United States bombed Iranian targets after three merchant ships were struck off Oman, Iran fired on Bahrain and Kuwait, and Brent crude jumped 6% while Treasury yields hit four-week highs and U.S. stock futures fell after President Trump, at the NATO summit in Turkey, called negotiating with Tehran a 'waste of time.'
business_politics.summary: The June ceasefire that ended the war between Israel, the United States, and Iran has unraveled into fresh tit-for-tat bombing across the Persian Gulf, reviving fears of a closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes.

sources.title: Trump Says Ceasefire With Iran Is Over After Latest Attacks
US and Iran trade strikes after attacks on tankers
Oil Prices Jump After Trump Says Ceasefire With Iran Is Over

business_politics.title: South Korea Enters Bear Market on AI-Chip Fears
business_politics.latest_developments: South Korea's Kospi index has fallen more than 20% below its June peak, entering a bear market, as investors turn on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix over doubts about the artificial-intelligence build-out.
business_politics.summary: The rout in the world's memory-chip heartland deepens a global selloff in AI-linked shares; Samsung and SK Hynix supply much of the high-bandwidth memory that powers data-center accelerators, so their slide signals waning confidence in AI capital spending.

sources.title: South Korea falls into bear market as traders fret over AI chipmakers' prospects

business.title: Larimer's Celebration Hall Moves Ahead
business.latest_developments: PublicSource detailed the plan as Food21 begins construction: event space, a food hall, and a demonstration kitchen backing local culinary entrepreneurs inside the former Larimer School's auditorium and gym.
business.summary: The nonprofit Food21 is converting the defunct Larimer School in Pittsburgh's Larimer neighborhood into a community venue called Celebration Hall, part of a broader push by developers there to build shared spaces after years of restoration.

sources.title: In Larimer, developers turn their focus to community spaces

business.title: Tangled Home Titles Snarl Allegheny County Families
business.latest_developments: A NEXTpittsburgh investigation put a face on the problem, following an East End woman named Veronica whose family lost a six-generation home in 2012 because the deed still sat in her grandmother's name after her 2002 death.
business.summary: Several thousand Allegheny County homes carry tangled or heirs' titles—deeds never transferred after an owner dies—leaving families unable to sell, repair, or borrow against houses they occupy and dragging down surrounding neighborhoods.

sources.title: Tangled titles on Allegheny County homes cause more problems than you realize

around_town.title: Parkway East Closes Friday for Bridge Swap
around_town.latest_developments: Two days out, PennDOT recommended that Pittsburgh-area employees work remotely during the closure and explained that Mammoet, the Dutch heavy-lift firm that moved the Chernobyl containment dome, will slide the new Commercial Street Bridge into place.
around_town.summary: PennDOT closes the Parkway East (Interstate 376) between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale interchange at 9 p.m. Friday, July 10, for 25 days to demolish and replace the aging Commercial Street Bridge on a road that carries about 100,000 vehicles a day.

sources.title: PennDOT recommending remote work for Pittsburgh employees during upcoming Parkway East closure
Here's how PennDOT is going to move the new Commercial Street Bridge into place on the Parkway East

around_town.title: West Mifflin Segment of Great Allegheny Passage to Close
around_town.latest_developments: A West Mifflin stretch of the Great Allegheny Passage will close for almost a month starting Thursday evening, July 9.
around_town.summary: The Great Allegheny Passage, the rail-trail linking Pittsburgh to Cumberland, Maryland, will lose its West Mifflin segment for roughly four weeks, forcing cyclists and walkers onto detours.

sources.title: West Mifflin segment of Greater Allegheny Passage to close

around_town.title: Youngwood Approves Emergency Depot Street Demolition
around_town.latest_developments: Youngwood officials approved a $325,000 emergency contract to tear down a structurally unsound building on Depot Street after a recent roof collapse.
around_town.summary: The Westmoreland County borough of Youngwood is racing to demolish a collapsing Depot Street structure it deemed a public-safety hazard.

sources.title: Youngwood approves $325K emergency demolition for collapsing Depot Street building

events.title: Pittsburgh CLO Stages 'Mean Girls'
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh CLO's summer production of the 'Mean Girls' musical is running now, and TribLive reviewed it as a sparkly summer girls' night out.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Civic Light Opera is presenting 'Mean Girls,' the musical Tina Fey adapted from her 2004 film comedy, which premiered on Broadway in 2018.

sources.title: Review: Pittsburgh CLO's 'Mean Girls' is a sparkly summer girls' night out

around_teams.title: Rod Woodson Joins Cam Heyward's Podcast
around_teams.latest_developments: Steelers Hall of Famer Rod Woodson appeared on Cam Heyward's 'Not Just Football,' recounting untold stories from his 17-year NFL career.
around_teams.summary: Woodson, the cornerback the Steelers drafted 10th overall in 1987 and a Pro Football Hall of Famer, sat down with current Steelers defensive lineman Cam Heyward for a career retrospective on Heyward's show.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: Rod Woodson Tells Untold Steelers Stories from His NFL Career & More! | Not Just Football

team_usa.title: USMNT World Cup Report Cards
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian graded the U.S. roster after the round-of-16 exit, handing high marks to midfielders Weston McKennie and Malik Tillman while Christian Pulisic and Sergiño Dest fell short.
team_usa.summary: The United States men's team crashed out of its home World Cup with a 4-1 loss to Belgium in Seattle, and post-mortems focus on uneven individual performances across Mauricio Pochettino's squad.

sources.title: USMNT World Cup player ratings: high marks for McKennie and Tillman, but Pulisic and Dest fall short

team_usa.title: EU Lawmakers Target Infantino Over Balogun Reversal
team_usa.latest_developments: Dozens of European Parliament lawmakers are gathering support to investigate FIFA president Gianni Infantino over his role in reinstating U.S. striker Folarin Balogun after a red card, a reversal that followed contact with President Trump.
team_usa.summary: Balogun's sending-off was suspended before the United States' round-of-16 match, and the intervention—linked to Trump's calls to Infantino—has drawn accusations that FIFA bent its rules for the host nation.

sources.title: EU lawmakers eye investigating FIFA's Infantino

team_usa.title: Pay-to-Play Blamed for U.S. World Cup Failure
team_usa.latest_developments: An ESPN examination argued America's early World Cup exit traces to its pay-to-play youth system, where families' ability to fund travel soccer outweighs player development.
team_usa.summary: As the United States men's team reckons with its round-of-16 loss to Belgium, critics point to a youth pipeline that prices out talent and prioritizes expensive travel leagues over developing the best players.

sources.title: Pay-to-play youth soccer explains America's World Cup losses

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: XBOX Cuts; Bundling and the Internet Solvent; Transaction, Coordination, and Sunk Costs
reading.summary: Ben Thompson reads Microsoft's big Xbox layoffs as proof its Game Pass subscription bundle failed, using the moment to explore how bundling, transaction costs, and sunk costs shape internet economics.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Let AI Burn
reading.summary: Zitron contends the AI industry is buckling under its own economics and argues observers should let the overhyped, unprofitable build-out fail rather than prop it up.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Beware of Productivity Paradoxes
reading.summary: Newport uses the personal computer, once seen as a productivity slam dunk, to show why new technologies often fail to deliver the gains they promise.
